The section 1.1 table also gives wheat as "120.21 | 2nd advance estimate, 2025–26 (record)".
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **2025-26 output beat the target.** The Ministry's Third Advance Estimates for 2025-26 were released 27–28 May 2026, before the post's 24 July 2026 information date. They put foodgrain output at a record 376.563 MT, above the 362.5 MT target.
  - **Crop figures:** rice 154.024 MT, wheat 120.657 MT, maize 55.093 MT.
  - **The 2024-25 base was revised.** These releases put 2024-25 at 357.732 MT, not the 353.96 MT in the post.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Time-Series-3rd-AE-2025-26-English.pdf
  - https://agronfoodprocessing.com/india-records-highest-ever-foodgrain-production-at-376-56-million-tons-in-2025-26/
  - https://www.socialnews.xyz/2026/05/27/indias-foodgrain-production-surges-to-all-time-high-of-376-563-million-tonnes-in-2025-26/
- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The Ministry of Agriculture's Third Advance Estimates for 2025-26 (released late May 2026) put foodgrain output at a record 376.56 MT, above the 362.5 MT target cited below, with wheat at 120.66 MT. The same release revised 2024-25 to 357.73 MT. The demand-floor argument below is unchanged; if anything, it is stronger."
- Confidence: several summaries agree on 376.56 MT, and one summary is of the desagri.gov.in PDF itself. The rice and 2024-25 base figures come from summaries only. This post's 2024-25 rice figure (151.84 MT) was not reconciled.

- Claim in post: "One senior industry official cautioned that the comfortable pricing window "may remain comfortable until August 2026, after which China could again start imposing stringent curbs."" The cost model also "identifies a crossover at approximately $10.3/MMBtu delivered gas price, solving (gas price × 30 MMBtu/tonne) + $110/tonne against the cheapest tender of this cycle, $419/t (Nov-25)."
- Current (as of 18 Oct 2026):
  - **Prices fell further after August.** Fertilizer Daily reported (7 Aug 2026) an RCF urea tender for up to 1.7 MT, shipping by 24 September. Per Profercy, the lowest offers were $390.25/t cfr east coast and $393.65/t cfr west coast. That is about 12% below the June NFL tender and below the $419/t this post calls the cycle's cheapest.
  - **China did not curb; it supplied.** Fertilizer Daily (7 Sep 2026), citing Bloomberg, said China was set to supply at least 1.2 MT to India under that tender. One summary put China's 2026 urea export allowance at about 5–5.5 MT.
  - **Final award not found.** No official RCF award notice was located.
  - Seen: summaries only.

  - https://www.fertilizerdaily.com/20260907-china-urea-india-tender-1-2-million-tonnes-2026/

Trade press (Fertilizer Daily, citing Profercy and Bloomberg) reported lowest offers of about $390–394/t cfr in RCF's August–September urea tender, with China expected to supply at least 1.2 MT. That is below the $419/t used here as the cycle's floor. By this piece's own formula, it would lower the gas-price crossover from about $10.3 to about $9.3/MMBtu. Final award prices were not confirmed."
- Confidence:
  - Offer levels: two trade-press summaries agree.
  - Award volume and price: unverified.
  - The $9.3/MMBtu figure is this blog's arithmetic, not a source figure.

refiners-won-exemption-fight-biofuels.text:

  - **EPA has acted on exemptions several times since the cases the post describes. The post (3 Oct 2026) mentions none of these actions.**
    - **22 Aug 2025:** EPA decided 175 petitions from 38 refineries for compliance years 2016–2024. It granted 63 in full and 77 in part (50%), denied 28 and found 7 ineligible. EPA's technical report puts the total exempted at 5,340 million RINs. One summary (ALL4) says EPA ruled on 16 more petitions by 7 Nov 2025.

  - **Reallocation is moving beyond 70%.** EPA said it would propose, before the end of October 2026, reallocating 100% of the difference between projected and actual 2025 exempted volumes into the 2026 and 2027 RVOs. OPIS describes this as a "proposed 100% reallocation into 2026, 2027 RVOs".
  - No result reported a D.C. Circuit ruling on the Set 2 petitions.
  - Seen: summaries only.

- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. EPA has acted on exemptions beyond the cases described here. In August 2025 it decided 175 petitions for 2016–2024, granting most of them in full or in part. sugar-at-5570-kilo-why-cane-acreage.text:
- Claim in post: "Separately, reports suggest India may need to import sugar for the first time in roughly a decade if the current stock trajectory holds." The post also says: "industry estimates put closing stock as of 30 September 2026 at just 3–3.5 million tonnes".

  - **The import decision had already been taken when the post went up (21 Aug 2026).** By a DGFT notification of 20 August 2026, the government allowed duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar under a tariff-rate quota, valid until 31 October 2026. The conditions reported:
    - only companies with in-house refining capacity may import;
    - the refined sugar must be sold in India by 31 October.
  - Coverage (Crisil, Business Today, News on AIR, Rural Voice) describes this as the first such imports for domestic use in about a decade.
  - In late August the industry said around 8 lakh tonnes of the quota had been allocated.
  - **The stock estimate is unchanged in substance.**
    - In late August ISMA projected closing stock at about 35 lakh tonnes at end-September. That is in line with the post's 3–3.5 million tonnes; one Crisil summary gives 3.9 MMT.
    - ISMA and NFCSF put 2025-26 net production at about 279 lakh tonnes after about 30 lakh tonnes was diverted to ethanol. Consumption is estimated at 280–285 lakh tonnes.
  - The existing 12 Oct note covers the price reversal and refers to "stock limits and other supply measures". It does not mention the import decision.
  - Seen: summaries only.
  - https://www.businesstoday.in/india/story/sugar-price-surge-govt-allows-1-million-tonne-duty-free-imports-ahead-of-festive-season-550462-2026-08-20
  - https://newsonair.gov.in/government-allows-duty-free-imports-of-10-lakh-tonnes-of-raw-sugar-until-31st-october/

  - https://eng.ruralvoice.in/india-allows-10-lakh-tonnes-of-duty-free-raw-sugar-imports-to-tame-record-prices

- Suggested wording: "Updated [date]. The import this piece described as a possibility had already been decided. A DGFT notification of 20 August 2026 allowed duty-free imports of 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar, by refiners only and valid until 31 October 2026, which press coverage describes as the first such imports for domestic use in about a decade. ISMA's late-August projection of about 35 lakh tonnes of closing stock at end-September is in line with the estimate quoted here."
- Confidence: several independent summaries agree on the 20 Aug date, the 10 lakh tonne quota and the 31 Oct validity.
